title: Inspector Pricing: Plans, Costs and Overages (2026)
summary: Inspector pricing is based on metered units tied to traffic, so your actual bill differs from the base plan price.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits in an Inspector setup


Don't expect Activepieces to replace Inspector or change what it meters. It sits beside it, carrying alerts to the places your team reads and watching the usage number that drives your bill, with unlimited flows on every plan, including free.


It's an automation tool, so it only helps where Inspector hands it something to act on.


### Routing Inspector alerts into your tools


When an Inspector alert needs to land somewhere other than Inspector's own dashboard, Activepieces reaches the destination through 750 integrations, roughly 60% of them community-contributed.


A flow starts from a trigger, and a webhook trigger gives Inspector's alert a place to arrive. From there the flow can post to Slack, send an email, or open a ticket, so the person on call sees the problem where they already work.


The catch is the hook. I can only point to what Inspector's documentation exposes, and I haven't confirmed a webhook or outbound notification option on every plan. Check that before you design anything around it.


If your plan has no outbound hook, the flow has nothing to start from, and the alert stays inside Inspector.


Activepieces meters the run, not the steps inside it: its pricing page charges 1 credit per flow run however many steps it has, where Zapier bills per task and Make per module.


A ten-step alert flow that fans out to Slack, email and a ticket costs the same single credit as a two-step shortcut, so splitting the work into smaller, more reliable steps never raises the bill.


The Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows, so count how many alerts your traffic produces and you know whether that covers you.


In the illustration below, an Inspector alert enters an Activepieces flow, which fans out to Slack, email and a ticket, while a dashed arrow from a usage-check step, itself 1 credit per run, joins the same flow.


Read it as one flow with two ways in, one for events Inspector pushes and one for a check you schedule.


### Watching usage before it hits the plan limit


The dashed arrow's the part that protects your bill. Because Inspector's price depends on the unit it meters, the number to watch is that unit's running total against your plan limit, not the headline price.


A scheduled flow in Activepieces can fetch that total and compare it to a threshold you set, then feed the result into the same Slack, email or ticket outputs.


Run once a day, that check uses about 30 of the Free plan's 1,000 monthly credits, so the free plan's monthly budget is essentially consumed by this single daily check.


This works only if Inspector exposes usage in a form a flow can read, such as an API endpoint. I haven't confirmed that it does.


If it doesn't, you're left with checking the billing page by hand, and the flow can at best remind you to do so on a schedule.


Where the data is available, a warning that arrives while you still have room is what separates a planned upgrade from a surprise overage. Set the threshold early enough that someone can act on it.
